_meta.update_note_22: 2026-10-08: added 8 test_meta.py POISONER entries (root-cause blocked, not failure-blocked) from run 37713861976 (PR 170538, torch_npu@79c55b42b0, pytorch@f49e82e147): these 8 cases PASSED, but their async device-side kernel failures poison the worker process context (first-unreported rule) and the error surfaces in the NEXT case of the same 100-case batch, which then gets wrongly failure-blocked by the auto-blocker. 4 kernel defects identified via plog: topk_float64 x3 directions (AICPU TopK errcode 21008 'inner error', retCode 0x2a), stft_complex128 (AICPU STFT exception), pad_reflect bfloat16/float16 x3 (aclnnReflectionPad2d MirrorPadAiCore tiling failure errno 561103/EZ1008), pad_replicate_bfloat16 dispatch_symbolic (PadV3 edge AICore task exception; op-plugin replication_pad2d -> PadV3 mode=edge). Proof that victim-only blocking does not prevent recurrence: run 37504481922's 10 victims were blocked (update_note_20) yet run 37713861976 produced 8 NEW victims (update_note_21, same cases as adjacent run 37712698624) from these same poisoners - collection-time filtering shifts batch boundaries and reassigns the victim each run. Blocking the poisoners removes the poisoning events themselves; the 8 victims would pass in a clean context. Residual risk: build drift (pytorch/torch_npu changes shift the per-test-name-hash-seeded deterministic sample inputs) may expose sibling dtype variants as new poisoners (run 37504481922's PadV3 poisoners were uint8/int8 replicate variants vs bfloat16 here) - add incrementally if new pad/topk/stft-family victims appear. Remove these 8 poisoners together with the update_note_21 victims after CANN/torch_npu fix the 4 kernel defects. Systemic fix: harness-side per-case torch.npu.synchronize() would attribute async failures to the submitting case so the auto-blocker blocks poisoners, not victims.
